title: Unparseable AVC SPS can cause an out-of-bounds read in OpenH264
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: The AVC coded-size scanner discarded SPS parsing errors, allowing malformed dimensions or cropping offsets to reach OpenH264. Decoding an untrusted AVC-coded HEIF can cause an out-of-bounds read, crash, or disclose mapped process memory through returned image planes or thumbnails.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-W4QT31RS. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: Fixed by rejecting unparseable SPS data in AVC/VVC size checks; included in libheif 1.23.7. The affected decoder-plugin configuration and user-controlled decode conditions are described in the advisory. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: Application must decode untrusted AVC-coded HEIF; disclosure depends on memory layout and a caller receiving the decoded image/thumbnail.
impacts.exploitation: The cited advisory does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.
